reviewed.disposition: writeJsonArtifact routes canonical operational paths through project scope and task transactions. writePortableJsonArtifact rejects canonical operational identities and active operational transactions before writing interchange/configuration files.
Writes .forgeloop/manifest.json installation ownership metadata after manifest validation and safe-path validation. This manifest describes shipped kit files, not task artifacts or event authority.

Named atomic writes publish explicit portable bundle attachment and event outputs. Native ledger bytes come from selected SQLite rows; retained filesystem ledger reads occur only in the unselected branch.

Writes selected canonical statement bytes to an OS temporary directory for external signing; refuses an active SQLite write transaction, rechecks canonical bytes after callback and removes the temporary directory in finally.

Named write publishes shipped template entries from TEMPLATE_PATHS with ownership planning and preservation. Reviewed TEMPLATE_PATHS contains kit documents, schemas and ignore rules, not live operational task artifacts.

Named writes publish managed kit templates and staged hidden-layout kit updates; source entries derive from TEMPLATE_PATHS. Hash verification precedes installation manifest authority changes. This role does not establish all migration writer coverage.
Named write restores missing managed kit template bytes and records installation ownership. Native stores bypass legacy transaction recovery; filesystem transaction repair remains explicitly refused.

Atomic JSON helper callers write repository-index engine-state.json for tgrep ownership/readiness. Paths are repository-index scoped and process ownership is inspected; these records are auxiliary search process metadata.

Writes user-scoped persistent-search process identity, nonce, endpoint and activity metadata; caller path source is the home-directory transport root. This is search transport coordination, not project task/ledger authority.

limitations: Source role review is bounded to named static writes and listed supporting sources. It does not prove alias, dynamic or external caller coverage.
Migration, backup and restore writer authority remains under review.
Search process metadata classification does not validate arbitrary callers supplying a statePath.
